This pathway highlights a direct molecular interaction between Bethanechol and the receptor, suggesting a role in modulating cholinergic signaling. Additionally, Bethanechol is associated with Hyoscyamine, an antimuscarinic agent that also binds to Chrm2, further supporting a broader role in muscarinic receptor regulation. The evidence from both paths indicates that Bethanechol may influence Chrm2 through muscarinic receptor activation, though the exact mechanism and extent of this interaction require further investigation. The integration of these pathways underscores the involvement of muscarinic receptors in the regulation of Chrm2, but the strength of the evidence remains moderate due to the indirect nature of the relationships.
